betareg

Fit beta regression with a cloglog mean link

Stata 

betareg share x, link(cloglog)

R betareg 

betareg::betareg(share~x,data=data,link="cloglog",type="ML",link.phi="log")

Differs from Stata Uses ordinary ML with a log link for precision, matching Stata slink(log). Without link.phi="log", betareg reports constant phi on the identity scale while Stata reports ln(phi). Responses must lie strictly inside (0,1).

Stata reference · R reference

Fit beta regression with a logit mean link

Stata 

betareg share x, link(logit)

R betareg 

betareg::betareg(share~x,data=data,link="logit",type="ML",link.phi="log")

Differs from Stata Uses ordinary ML with a log link for precision, matching Stata slink(log). Without link.phi="log", betareg reports constant phi on the identity scale while Stata reports ln(phi). Responses must lie strictly inside (0,1).

Stata reference · R reference

Differs from Stata Uses ordinary ML with a log link for precision, matching Stata slink(log). Without link.phi="log", betareg reports constant phi on the identity scale while Stata reports ln(phi). Responses must lie strictly inside (0,1).

Model beta-regression precision using a covariate

Stata 

betareg share x, scale(z) slink(log)

R betareg 

betareg::betareg(share~x|z,data=data,link="logit",link.phi="log",type="ML")

Differs from Stata Uses a log link for precision; align Stata scale-link parameterization before numerical comparison.

bsqreg

Bootstrap quantile-regression inference

Stata 

bsqreg y x z, reps(99)

R quantreg 

{ fit <- quantreg::rq(y~x+z,data=data,tau=0.5); summary(fit,se="boot",R=99) }

Differs from Stata Uses 99 bootstrap replications for quantile-regression inference. R and Stata random streams and resampling implementations differ, so bootstrap standard errors will not be identical.

Stata reference · R reference

cloglog

Fit cloglog regression

Stata 

cloglog b x z

R stats 

stats::glm(b ~ x + z,data=data,family=stats::binomial(link="cloglog"))

Differs from Stata R uses the complementary log-log link. Match the event category and complete cases; the GLM result object and convergence tolerances differ from Stata cloglog.

Stata reference · R reference

Fit cloglog without an intercept

Stata

R stats 

stats::glm(b ~ x + z - 1,data=data,family=stats::binomial(link="cloglog"))

Differs from Stata R uses the complementary log-log link. Match the event category and complete cases; the GLM result object and convergence tolerances differ from Stata cloglog.

constraint

Represent a linear equality constraint as a matrix

Stata 

constraint define 1 x = z

R stats 

L <- matrix(c(0,1,-1),nrow=1,dimnames=list(NULL,c("intercept","x","z")))

Fixed workflow: L beta = 0 encodes equal x and z coefficients. A fitting routine must enforce the constraint.

Stata reference · R reference

fracreg

Fit fractional logit regression with sandwich inference

Stata 

fracreg logit share x

R sandwich 

{ fit <- stats::glm(share ~ x,data=data,family=stats::quasibinomial(link="logit")); lmtest::coeftest(fit,vcov.=sandwich::vcovHC(fit,type="HC0"),df=Inf) }

Differs from Stata Quasi-binomial fit avoids a noninteger-success warning. Sandwich inference is explicit; finite-sample corrections can differ.

Stata reference · R reference

Fit fractional probit regression with sandwich inference

Stata 

fracreg probit share x

R sandwich 

{ fit <- stats::glm(share ~ x,data=data,family=stats::quasibinomial(link="probit")); lmtest::coeftest(fit,vcov.=sandwich::vcovHC(fit,type="HC0"),df=Inf) }

Differs from Stata Quasi-binomial fit avoids a noninteger-success warning. Sandwich inference is explicit; finite-sample corrections can differ.

glm

Fit a gamma log-link model for positive outcomes

Stata 

glm y x z, family(gamma) link(log)

R stats 

stats::glm(y ~ x + z, data=data, family=stats::Gamma(link="log"))

Differs from Stata The family and link are explicit. R and Stata can use different dispersion scaling and reference tests even when fitted means agree; align the sample and scale option before comparing standard errors.

hetregress

Fit a normal mean model with multiplicative heteroskedasticity

Stata 

hetregress y x, het(z)

R nlme 

nlme::gls(y~x,data=data,weights=nlme::varExp(form=~z),method="ML")

Differs from Stata nlme models SD as exp(theta*z), so the coefficient on z in Stata log variance is 2*theta.

Stata reference · R reference

intreg

Fit normal regression to interval-valued outcomes

Stata 

intreg lower upper x z

R survival 

survival::survreg(survival::Surv(lower,upper,type="interval2")~x+z,data=data,dist="gaussian")

Differs from Stata Uses survreg as a Gaussian interval-likelihood engine for a cross-sectional outcome, without a time-to-event interpretation.

Report logistic odds ratios

Stata 

logistic b x z

R parameters 

{ fit <- stats::glm(b ~ x + z, data = data, family = stats::binomial()); parameters::model_parameters(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, ci_method = "wald") }

Differs from Stata Exponentiated coefficients with delta-method SEs, exponentiated Wald limits and original-link tests.

mlexp

Maximize an explicitly defined normal likelihood

Stata 

mlexp (lnnormalden(y,{mu},exp({lnsigma})))

R stats 

stats::optim(c(mu=mean(data$y),log_sigma=log(stats::sd(data$y))),function(par) -sum(stats::dnorm(data$y,mean=par[1],sd=exp(par[2]),log=TRUE)),method="BFGS",hessian=TRUE)

Differs from Stata R optimizes log sigma to enforce positivity; translate the scale parameter back using exp().

Stata reference · R reference

mlogit

Fit multinomial logit with a chosen reference outcome

Stata 

mlogit g x z, baseoutcome(4)

R nnet 

nnet::multinom(stats::relevel(factor(g), ref = "4") ~ x+z,data=data,trace=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Relevels outcome category 4 to the first R factor level, matching baseoutcome(4). Coefficient labels and optimization criteria differ; keep the same observations and category support.

Stata reference · R reference

Report standardized linear regression slopes

Stata 

regress y x z, beta

R stats 

{ fit <- stats::lm(y ~ x + z, data = data); sample <- stats::model.frame(fit); stats::coef(fit)[c("x", "z")] * vapply(sample[c("x", "z")], stats::sd, numeric(1)) / stats::sd(sample$y) }

Differs from Stata Numeric slopes use complete-case estimation-sample SDs; ordinary OLS inference remains in fit.

Stata reference · R reference

Use one-way clustered standard errors with cluster degrees of freedom

Stata 

regress y x z, vce(cluster g)

R sandwich 

{ fit <- stats::lm(y ~ x + z, data = data, subset = !is.na(g)); lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = ~g, type = "HC1"), df = length(unique(stats::expand.model.frame(fit, ~g)$g)) - 1L) }

Differs from Stata Only three clusters in this demonstration fixture; substantive applications need adequate independent clusters.

Stata reference · R reference
